companyDescription: AI GPU · Dominant Blackwell/Vera Rubin AI training + inference chips + CUDA ecosystem — picks & shovels of the AI buildout
priceNote: Trading $202.78, down from $204.12 prior close — caught in the broader semiconductor selloff (SOX -10.8%, $1.3T sector value erased on AI-capex-sustainability fears) despite 21-of-23-quarter beat streak intact.
summary: NVDA sold off alongside the broader AI-semis complex on capex-sustainability fears even though nothing company-specific broke — consensus target $263-274 now implies ~32% upside from $202.78, near the widest re-rating gap of the past year. Vera Rubin (HBM4, 3nm) ships to hyperscalers in H2 2026, and fiscal Q2 FY27 earnings land Aug 26. The company has beaten estimates in 21 of the last 23 quarters; the real swing factor is how much it beats by, not whether it beats.

catalysts.name: Fiscal Q2 FY27 Earnings
catalysts.description: First earnings since the July 2026 AI-capex-fear selloff. Market wants confirmation that hyperscaler orders (Jensen Huang cited ~$1T in cumulative Blackwell/Vera Rubin purchase orders through 2027 at GTC) are holding, not just guidance language.

catalysts.name: Vera Rubin H2 2026 Shipments
catalysts.description: HBM4 + 3nm architecture begins shipping to early-access hyperscaler customers in H2 2026 — the generational efficiency leap analysts are watching for roadmap-execution proof.

catalysts.name: Mag-7 Capex Read-Through (GOOGL/MSFT/META earnings)
catalysts.description: Hyperscaler Q2 earnings in late July are the nearest concrete data point on whether AI capex guidance holds — a direct read on NVDA's largest customer cohort ahead of its own Aug 26 print.

risks: AI-capex-sustainability debate is sector-wide, not NVDA-specific — BofA's Bubble Risk Indicator at 0.91 and comparisons to dot-com valuations could keep multiples compressed even if fundamentals hold
Hawkish Fed dot-plot shift (median 2026 projection raised, 9 of 19 officials see another hike) pressures long-duration AI multiples independent of NVDA execution
Vera Rubin ramp timing risk — any slip in H2 2026 hyperscaler shipments would remove the next roadmap-execution catalyst
China export-control precedent (H20 restrictions triggered a $4.5B charge and ~4% single-day drop in the prior cycle) — policy risk remains binary and outside company control
Post-earnings moves have historically been modest (median +0.3% day-1, +3.3% week-1) — don't expect a single print to close the 32% valuation gap quickly
Enterprise AI budget pushback and hyperscaler capacity resale (e.g., Meta selling spare AI compute) could signal early demand softening

estimateDates.note: Key test: do hyperscaler orders and Vera Rubin commentary confirm the $1T cumulative purchase-order figure from GTC
First hyperscaler shipments of HBM4/3nm Vera Rubin platform — roadmap-execution proof point

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held 3.50–3.75% for a 4th straight meeting (Jun 17, 2026). Next FOMC Jul 28–29 — CME FedWatch prices ~89% probability of another hold, but the June dot plot shifted the median 2026 projection higher, now leaning toward a hike rather than a cut.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Inflation still running above the 2% target; the hawkish dot-plot shift removes a rate-cut tailwind AI/growth stocks had been pricing in.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: High-multiple AI/semis names are the most rate-sensitive corner of the market — a hawkish surprise compresses long-duration growth multiples faster than it shows up in earnings, compounding the current capex-fear selloff.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — no imminent hike, but the FOMC Jul 28-29 decision lands just before NVDA's Aug 26 earnings, and a hawkish surprise would add multiple-compression risk on top of the sector-wide capex debate.

entryStrategy.verdict: BUY the capex-fear reset — scale in at $203, add on dip to $185-190. Target $231-268 as Aug 26 earnings confirm hyperscaler demand is intact.

catalystSpot.preRunup: NVDA's post-earnings moves have historically been modest and not correlated with beat magnitude — the stock's real driver has been the medium-term trend (median +11.1% over the following quarter, +87.6% over the following year) rather than the print itself.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: Muted in the days immediately pre-earnings; the multi-month trend matters more

postWin.note: NVDA has beaten consensus in 21 of the last 23 quarters. Post-print moves are typically modest short-term (median +0.3% day-1) but compound over the following quarter (+11.1% median) as guidance gets digested — the print itself rarely closes a valuation gap in one session.

postLose.note: NVDA fell ~4% in a single session on H200/China shipment-delay concerns ahead of Q1 FY26 results, and separately took a $4.5B charge tied to H20 export-license requirements — the closest comparable 'bad news' reactions, both policy-driven rather than demand-driven.

spotSizing.reason: BUY verdict, Strong Buy consensus, and a re-rating gap driven by sector-wide macro fear rather than company-specific deterioration — size at 8% initial given the mega-cap liquidity and dated Aug 26 catalyst, add on dip rather than chasing.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Below recent selloff support — would suggest the capex-fear narrative is deepening, not just a sentiment air-pocket

stopPostCatalyst.note: If Aug 26 guidance disappoints AND management can't confirm Vera Rubin hyperscaler orders, exit — that would be a genuine demand signal, not macro noise
